codeReview.summary: Clean, correct implementation that replaces generation-counter change detection with per-type dirty entity tracking. The O(all_entities * type_ids) scan is eliminated in favor of O(dirty_entities) iteration. All expectedBehavior requirements are met. The implementation has survived 3 subsequent commits to katla_ecs without regression.

issues.description: Stale docstring on clear_changed(): 'Snapshots the current maximum generation for each component type' should say 'Clears dirty entity sets for all component storages'. The second paragraph is still accurate. This is purely a documentation issue — the implementation is correct.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The dirty entity tracking design uses SparseSet<EntityId, ()> (unit value type) rather than a HashSet. This mirrors the existing SparseSet infrastructure already used for component storage. This pattern is now documented in architecture.md under 'ECS Change Detection'.

get_mut() marks entities as dirty even if the caller doesn't actually modify the component (conservative marking). This is an intentional design choice documented in the docstring at storage.rs:60-61. Tests like test_change_detection_overhead account for this.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: katla_ecs/src/storage.rs:60 — 'Marks the entity as changed for change detection, even if the component is not actually modified.'

summary: The feature correctly implements VAL-ECS-006: change detection is now O(dirty_entities) instead of O(all_entities * type_ids). The generation counter system (generations SparseSet + changed_generations HashMap) was cleanly replaced with a per-type dirty: SparseSet<EntityId, ()>. collect_changed_entity_ids() now iterates only dirty entities from the queried type storages. The old entities_with_components() full scan is no longer used by change detection. All 97 tests pass, clippy is clean, and the implementation survived 3 subsequent commits. One non-blocking docstring issue: clear_changed() still references 'maximum generation' instead of 'dirty sets'.
